page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features a 35 MB L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and BMI2, providing support for vectorized computation and cryptography workloads.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput delivers a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, while no local instance storage is bundled, requiring the attachment of remote block storage volumes for persistent data. Hardware accelerators are not present, with zero GPUs allocated to this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.c6.8xlarge consistently within the middle tier across most multi-core and memory evaluations. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,181.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 27,240.11, alongside 27,992.16 on stress-ng multi-core testing. In-memory operations scored moderately with 26.78 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and uncached memory read bandwidth of 109.69 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance trails lower, as indicated by weak percentiles in single-core stress-ng tests and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.88 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory ratio provides cost efficiency for compute-heavy architectures that do not require extensive memory footprints. However, the absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on network-attached storage, which must be factored into storage-intensive pipelines. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation tasks, static web serving tiers, batch compute jobs, and distributed backend services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor under the KVM hypervisor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is allocated 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 core-to-memory distribution. It provides a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate reliable mid-tier multi-threaded execution, registering 10,181.0 points on Geekbench multi-core and 27.992.16 on stress-ng multi-core tests, contrasted by lower single-core throughput. Given its compute density and lack of local disks, ecs.c6.8xlarge is well aligned for distributed microservices, static web serving, software build pipelines, and parallel batch processing.
